questions.question: How does the firm allocate capacity-constrained private fund and co-investment opportunities among client families?

The Head of Private Investments documents it, the CCO reviews each allocation before commitments are submitted, and employees participate only after eligible families' demand is met.

questions.question: How does the firm control trading in securities of public companies at which a member of a client family is an officer, director or 10% holder?
questions.expected: Such issuers are placed on a Client-Affiliated Issuer List maintained by the CCO. No transaction in their securities may be made for any client account or employee Reportable Account without the CCO's prior approval, and the de minimis exemption does not apply. Trades for the affiliated family member's own accounts also require written confirmation that the trade is permitted under the issuer's trading window or a Rule 10b5-1 plan and that Rule 144 or Section 16 filings will be made.
questions.quote: The CCO maintains a Client-Affiliated Issuer List of public companies of which a member of a client family is an officer, director or beneficial owner of 10% or more of any class of equity securities. No transaction in a security of an issuer on the Client-Affiliated Issuer List may be effected for any client account or Reportable Account without the prior approval of the CCO.
